{
  "edges": [
    {
      "fromKey": "n-ufqg50",
      "toKey": "n-sqwzjg",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The event of maintenance being deferred (work paused) is consistent with the condition that there is no evidence of a communication breakdown. The lack of documented confirmation or specific message content does not cause the pause; rather, the absence of such records leaves the status unknown but supported by the fact that work was paused due to an air-low indication.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": ["24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1"],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If a communication breakdown had occurred, it might have delayed the pause or response. However, evidence shows work was paused promptly (~10:02) after indication (~10:00), suggesting no critical failure in immediate comms.",
      "competingExplanation": "The air-low alarm triggered an automatic procedural response (pause work). The lack of documented communication breakdown is a gap in records, not evidence that one occurred. Competing explanation: No breakdown; standard procedure followed but documentation incomplete.","evidenceGap":"Need explicit record or witness testimony confirming whether messages were exchanged between Utilities and RHOB at 10:00-10:02 to distinguish 'no communication' from 'communication without recording'. The current evidence only shows the alarm occurred, work paused, and pressure restored. It does not show what was said."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-j8rnx",
      "toKey": "n-11gg5pk",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "Upstream pressure P-U remained stable (~6.9 bar) while downstream RHOB received low pressure, indicating a localized issue in the distribution path or at receiving equipment H-R. This supports the hypothesis of an unrecorded service-routing change (e.g., valve closed remotely, line isolated without ECP update).",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": ["fcd254db-75b3-4a9d-abec-44c5b6a9b34e#1"],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If the pressure loss were due to a compressor failure, upstream P-U would likely have dropped or C-11 RUN bit behavior would differ. Since P-U is stable and AL-44 maps to P-R (not COMP), this points downstream.",
      "competingExplanation": "Competing explanation: A physical blockage or leak in the distribution line between North gallery and RHOB, not a routing change. Both are plausible without valve-state evidence.","evidenceGap":"Need access to real-time pressure waveform data across all segments (North gallery -> Dryer aisle -> East rack -> RHOB) during 09:48-10:07 to locate the exact point of failure or isolation event. Also need historical ECP revision logs for this boundary between March and May."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-oigq1p",
      "toKey": "n-i3yme8",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "The work package cover had a blank temporary instruction attachment field at issue time. This supports the hypothesis that an unrecorded service-routing change (or undocumented valve state) existed without proper ECP revision or temporary instruction, creating a unique hazard scenario during boundary preparation.",
      "status": "unknown",
      "sourceIds": ["eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078"],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If the blank field meant no change occurred, then why did pressure drop? If it means a change was made but not recorded, that explains the hazard. Absence of attachment does not prove absence of change.",
      "competingExplanation": "Competing explanation: The blank field indicates standard procedure (no temporary instruction needed) and the pressure loss was due to equipment failure unrelated to routing changes.","evidenceGap":"Need engineering disposition records for any ECP revisions or service-routing changes affecting RHOB boundary between 2024-03-01 and May 20, 2024. Also need physical inspection of valve positions at H-R during the event."
    }
  ],
  "decision": {
    "summary": "The investigation identifies three primary causal branches: (1) No evidence of communication breakdown but work paused due to alarm; (2) Stable upstream pressure suggests localized downstream issue, possibly unrecorded routing change or valve state; (3) Blank temporary instruction field supports hypothesis of undocumented hazard scenario. All remain hypotheses pending additional evidence.",
    "evidenceUsed": [
      "n-ufqg50",
      "n-j8rnx",
      "n-oigq1p"
    ],
    "unknowns": [
      "Actual valve states at H-R during event",
      "Whether any service-routing change occurred between March and May 2024",
      "Content of verbal communications between Utilities and RHOB at 10:00-10:02"
    ],
    "alternatives": [
      "Pressure loss due to equipment failure (e.g., dryer malfunction) rather than routing change.",
      "Communication breakdown did occur but was not recorded."
    ],"confidence":0.65},"evidenceRequests":[
      "requestId\":\"req-1\",\"sourceId\":\"eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#2\",\"claimRef\":\"n-i3yme8\",\"question\":\"Provide engineering disposition records for any ECP revisions or service-routing changes affecting RHOB boundary between 2024-03-01 and May 20, 2024.","rationale\":\"To verify whether an unrecorded change occurred that created a unique hazard scenario."
    ]}
